title: Auto Loans: what remains unpaid on the earliest installment in arrears
content:
# Auto Loans: what remains unpaid on the earliest installment in arrears

This rule of the Auto Loans product category at PCB fixes how much of an installment is still unpaid when a borrower asks PCB to pay the earliest installment in arrears on an auto loan by a transfer from the borrower's own PCB checking account.

## Clauses

1. **Which installment.** The installment paid is the one whose installment date is the loan's next payment date as shown on the loan record.
2. **Standing credit.** The standing credit toward that installment is the sum of the amounts of the scheduled payments already applied toward the same installment date, less the amount of any such payment that was later returned unpaid.
3. **Which payment counts as returned.** A returned payment, for this purpose, is the payment named by the most recent payment reversal on the loan. Its amount comes off the standing credit only when it is itself a scheduled payment applied toward that same installment date.
4. **Installment remainder.** The installment remainder is the monthly payment less the standing credit, and it is never below zero.

## Steps

1. Read the loan's next payment date; that date identifies the installment.
2. Add up the scheduled payments applied toward that installment date.
3. Find the most recent payment reversal on the loan and the payment it names; if that payment is among the payments in step 2, take its amount off.
4. Subtract the standing credit from the monthly payment; a figure below zero counts as zero.

## Worked case (hypothetical loan)

Monthly payment 486.20; next payment date 2027-04-12. Scheduled payments applied toward 2027-04-12: 200.00 and 286.20. The most recent payment reversal on the loan names the 286.20 payment.

- Standing credit: 200.00 plus 286.20, less 286.20, that is 200.00.
- Installment remainder: 486.20 less 200.00, that is 286.20.

## Contrast cases

| Variation on the worked case | Standing credit | Installment remainder |
|---|---|---|
| The most recent reversal names a payment applied toward an earlier installment date | 486.20 | 0.00 |
| No reversal exists on the loan | 486.20 | 0.00 |
| Only the 200.00 payment exists, and no reversal names it | 200.00 | 286.20 |
| Scheduled payments of 500.00 toward that date, none returned | 500.00 | 0.00, never below zero |

**Wrong reading:** "every payment ever returned on the loan is taken off." **Correct basis:** the returned payment is the one named by the most recent payment reversal, and it matters only if it was applied toward this installment date.
